abstract: Reproducible and testable analytical performance of mass spectrometers is critical for inter-laboratory concordance of quantitative lipidomics analyses. However, common instrument readout or analyses of arbitrarily chosen lipid mixtures do not lend themselves to direct comparison between instruments independently configured and operated in different laboratories under in-house settings. We developed and validated the QC Shotgun workflow and web-accessible software that enable rapid testing, evaluation, documentation, and longitudinal monitoring of the performance of high-resolution mass spectrometers in quantitative shotgun lipidomics. Completed in less than 5 minutes, the QC Shotgun test reports 8 relative metric indices that facilitate inter-laboratory comparison and longitudinal assessment of instrument performance and identify deficiencies that are not apparent from instrument readouts. Systematic documentation of instrument status can improve inter-laboratory consistency and interpretation confidence of lipidomics datasets.
